name: Pediatric posterolateral approach to the distal tibia
corridor: Just lateral to Achilles, through medial border of peroneal muscles with peroneals retracted laterally to expose posterior tibia

positioning.text: Position prone or lateral with posterior ankle accessible and fluoroscopy preconfigured for AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views.

setup.text: Use CT to confirm posterior fragment morphology, mark physis and sural nerve course, and plan whether tibia alone or tibia and fibula require exposure.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark lateral Achilles border, fibular tip, distal-tibial and fibular physes, sural-nerve course, and posterior joint line.

incision.text: Make a longitudinal incision approximately 0.5 cm lateral and parallel to lateral Achilles border, centered on posterior pathology.

superficial_interval.text: Raise full-thickness flaps, identify/protect sural nerve, and expose peroneal muscles.

deep_interval.text: Develop medial border of peroneal muscles and retract them laterally to expose posterior and posterolateral distal-tibial fragments.

layers.text: Skin, sural-nerve plane, peroneal fascia, medial peroneal border, posterior periosteum/capsule, then posterior distal tibia.

structures_encountered.text: Sural nerve, short saphenous vein, peroneal muscles/tendons, Achilles tendon border, distal physes, posterior capsule, and posterior fragments are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Sural nerve, short saphenous vein, peroneal tendons, posterior tibial neurovascular structures medially, physes/perichondral rings, periosteum, and cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Identify sural nerve before proximal extension and keep dissection immediately along medial peroneal border without drifting toward posteromedial bundle.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract peroneals gently laterally and avoid forceful medial retraction or circumferential fragment/physeal stripping.

exposure.text: Provides direct access to posterior and posterolateral distal-tibial fragments and can reach posterior distal fibula.

limitations.text: Anterior and medial articular fragments are not directly visualized and posterior pediatric structures constrain medial extension.

extensions.text: Extend along either side of identified sural nerve or add a separate fragment-directed anterior/medial incision when necessary.

indications.text: Use for displaced posterior/posterolateral distal-tibial physeal or transitional fragments requiring direct reduction and buttress fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose anterior or medial exposure for dominant nonposterior pathology or when posterior skin/positioning is unsafe.

implant_implications.text: Use fragment-specific posterior fixation that avoids physis, joint, peroneal tendons, and posteromedial bundle; maintain enough soft-tissue coverage over hardware.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm posterior reduction, physeal alignment, mortise congruity, and implant containment on AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views.

closure.text: Return peroneal muscles anatomically, close deep fascia only without tension, ensure sural nerve is free, and close skin in layers.

complications.text: Complications include sural neuropathy, peroneal-tendon irritation, wound problems, physeal arrest, angular deformity, infection, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Add a separate fragment-directed incision when anterior/medial reduction cannot be confirmed rather than extending across protected posterior structures.

procedure_applications.condition: A displaced posterior or posterolateral distal-tibial fragment requires direct reduction
Posterior distal-fibular access is required with posterior tibial exposure

questions.question: Where is incision relative to Achilles?
questions.answer: About 0.5 cm lateral and parallel to lateral Achilles border.
